notes.title: zvec
notes.ai_summary: Zvec is an open-source, in-process vector database built by Alibaba, offering lightning-fast similarity search with support for dense and sparse vectors, full-text search, and hybrid queries. It is designed for easy embedding into applications, making it ideal for RAG pipelines, LLM memory, and local semantic search with minimal setup and production-grade reliability.

todo_items.text: Explore the group-by search and random rotation quantization features introduced in v0.6.0 for improved recall and efficiency.
Benchmark Zvec against other embedded vector databases like FAISS or Chroma for your specific use case.
Integrate Zvec as a local vector store for an LLM memory or RAG pipeline using its Python or Node.js bindings.
Review the documentation on hybrid search and full-text search to leverage combined filtering capabilities.
Check the project roadmap and consider contributing to upcoming features or bug fixes.

notes.title: qlora
notes.ai_summary: QLoRA is an efficient finetuning method that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter LLM on a single 48GB GPU using 4-bit quantization and Low Rank Adapters (LoRA). It achieves state-of-the-art chatbot performance while dramatically lowering hardware requirements, making LLM research more accessible. The repository provides code, pretrained adapter weights, and interactive demos for immediate experimentation.

todo_items.text: Try the live demo to see Guanaco's performance firsthand.
Run the Colab notebook for finetuning a small model (e.g., 7B) to understand the workflow.
Read the paper to grasp the technical innovations (NF4, Double Quantization, Paged Optimizers).
Explore the adapter weights and evaluate on a custom dataset.
Contribute by testing with different base models (e.g., LLaMA 2) and reporting issues.

notes.title: fastapi
notes.ai_summary: FastAPI is a high-performance Python web framework for building APIs, leveraging standard Python type hints for automatic validation, serialization, and interactive documentation. It is built on Starlette and Pydantic, making it fast, easy to use, and production-ready. Its popularity and active community make it an essential tool for modern Python API development.

todo_items.text: Run the official 'First Steps' tutorial to create a basic FastAPI app
Explore the auto-generated interactive API documentation (Swagger UI and ReDoc)
Review the performance benchmarks comparing FastAPI to other frameworks

notes.title: finetune
notes.ai_summary: Finetune is a Python library that provides a scikit-learn-style API for fine-tuning state-of-the-art pretrained NLP models (BERT, RoBERTa, GPT, etc.) using TensorFlow. It aims to simplify the workflow of adapting large language models to custom classification, regression, sequence labeling, and other downstream tasks, making it appealing for developers familiar with scikit-learn.

todo_items.text: Evaluate compatibility with modern TensorFlow versions (2.x) as the library may rely on older TF 1.x APIs.
Consider porting key model implementations to PyTorch or provide a PyTorch backend to align with the current NLP ecosystem (Hugging Face Transformers).
Check for open issues and pull requests; merge or close stale ones to improve community trust.
Add examples and documentation for fine-tuning with recently released models like GPT-3, LLaMA, or other transformer variants.
Explore integration with modern training frameworks (e.g., Lightning, Ray) to simplify distributed training and hyperparameter tuning.

notes.title: ktransformers
notes.ai_summary: KTransformers is a flexible framework for efficient LLM inference and fine-tuning using CPU-GPU heterogeneous computing. It supports a wide range of modern LLMs and integrates with popular tools like LLaMA-Factory and SGLang, making it a valuable resource for both experimentation and production deployment.

todo_items.text: Set up ktransformers environment and run basic inference on a supported model
Explore heterogeneous CPU-GPU expert scheduling to optimize performance
Test fine-tuning workflow using LLaMA-Factory integration
Review roadmap and consider contributing to new model support

notes.title: langchain
notes.ai_summary: LangChain is a popular, open-source framework for building LLM-powered applications and AI agents, offering modular components and integrations to simplify development. It is widely adopted in the AI community and serves as the foundation for many production systems, making it a critical tool for anyone working with large language models.

todo_items.text: Explore LangGraph for advanced agent orchestration and stateful workflows
Try Deep Agents for pre-built agent patterns like planning and subagents
Integrate with your preferred LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.)
Review the extensive third-party integrations for tools and data sources

notes.title: dify
notes.ai_summary: Dify is an open-source platform for building and deploying AI-powered agentic workflows and RAG pipelines. It features a low-code/no-code interface, supports a wide range of AI models, and offers flexible deployment options. This project is essential for teams looking to quickly prototype and productionize AI applications without rebuilding infrastructure.

todo_items.text: Explore the self-hosted deployment option to understand infrastructure requirements and flexibility.
Experiment with building a custom RAG pipeline using your own data to evaluate performance.
Contribute to the project by improving multilingual documentation or adding new tool integrations.

notes.title: airllm
notes.ai_summary: AirLLM is a memory-efficient inference tool that enables running large language models (up to 70B on a 4GB GPU, 405B on 8GB, and even 671B DeepSeek-V3 on ~12GB) without quantization, distillation, or pruning. It supports a wide range of popular open-source models (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, ChatGLM, etc.) and is actively maintained with regular updates and community engagement. This project is highly valuable for developers who want to experiment with or deploy large LLMs on limited hardware.

todo_items.text: Try running a 70B model (e.g., Llama 3 70B) on a 4GB GPU using AirLLM to verify the core functionality.
Test compatibility with your specific model or use case (e.g., fine-tuned checkpoints, custom vocab) by following the Quickstart guide.
Explore the model compression feature (3x speed up) and compare performance vs. raw inference.
Contribute to the project by reporting issues or submitting PRs for additional model support or documentation improvements.

notes.title: milvus
notes.ai_summary: Milvus is a high-performance, cloud-native vector database built for scalable approximate nearest neighbor search, supporting hybrid search and real-time updates. It is essential for AI applications like RAG and multimodal search, with active development and a strong community, making it a top choice for vector storage and similarity search.

todo_items.text: Set up a standalone instance using Docker to quickly test Milvus.
Explore Milvus Lite for lightweight Python integration and prototyping.
Read the architecture overview to understand distributed mode and scalability.
Review the Python SDK documentation for connecting and performing CRUD operations.
Test search performance with your own embedding dataset to evaluate suitability.

notes.title: pymilvus
notes.ai_summary: PyMilvus is the official Python SDK for Milvus, the open-source vector database designed for scalable similarity search and AI applications. It provides a comprehensive API for managing collections, indexing, and performing vector operations, making it essential for developers integrating Milvus with Python.

todo_items.text: Check the compatibility table in the README to ensure your PyMilvus version matches your Milvus server version
Run the quickstart example from the documentation to verify connectivity and basic operations
Review the changelog and API differences when upgrading to a newer version (e.g., 2.6.x)
Explore advanced features like IVF or HNSW index parameters for performance tuning
Contribute to the project by reporting issues or submitting pull requests on GitHub

notes.title: ms-swift
notes.ai_summary: ms-swift is a scalable framework for fine-tuning and deploying large language models and multimodal large models, supporting 600+ LLMs and 400+ MLLMs with techniques like PEFT, full-parameter training, and RL algorithms (GRPO, DPO). It integrates advanced parallelism (Megatron) and provides a full pipeline from training to inference and quantization, making it a versatile tool for researchers and practitioners.

todo_items.text: Install ms-swift with dependencies using 'pip install ms-swift[all]' or follow platform-specific instructions.
Run a quick start example from the documentation to verify setup and understand basic usage.
Review the supported model list and select a target model for your use case (e.g., Qwen3, DeepSeek).
Explore advanced training configurations (Megatron parallelism, GRPO algorithms) for large-scale experiments.
Join community channels (Discord, WeChat) for support and to stay updated with developments.

notes.title: node
notes.ai_summary: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime that enables server-side scripting and event-driven, non-blocking I/O. It is widely used for building scalable network applications and is supported by a large ecosystem of packages via npm. The project has a strong governance model and is actively maintained with regular releases and long-term support.

notes.title: ollama
notes.ai_summary: Ollama is a popular open-source tool to run large language models locally with ease. It provides a simple CLI, REST API, and integrates with many AI assistants and development tools. It supports a wide range of models like Gemma, DeepSeek, and Qwen, making local AI accessible.

Explore the REST API documentation to integrate Ollama into custom applications

notes.title: tau2-bench
notes.ai_summary: Tau2-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM-based agents in tool-agent-user interactions across real-world domains like airline, retail, and banking. It includes knowledge retrieval and voice full-duplex evaluation, with a live leaderboard at taubench.com. The project is actively maintained and provides a standardized framework for agent evaluation.

notes.title: inference
notes.ai_summary: Xinference is a powerful Python library for serving open-source LLMs, speech recognition, and multimodal models through a unified API compatible with OpenAI. It supports deployment on cloud, on-prem, or local environments, making it easy to swap between models with minimal code changes. With features like auto-batching and agent-native serving, it provides a production-ready inference platform.

Explore agent-native serving with Xagent for dynamic planning and tool use

notes.title: jcode
notes.ai_summary: jcode is a Rust-based CLI/TUI harness for AI coding agents, designed to maximize RAM efficiency while enabling intelligent code generation. notes.title: open-code-review
notes.ai_summary: Open Code Review is an AI-powered CLI tool for code review, combining deterministic rules (e.g., NPE, XSS) with LLM agents to deliver precise line-level comments on Git diffs. Battle-tested at Alibaba scale, it supports OpenAI and Anthropic models, achieving high precision with low token consumption. This makes it a robust, production-ready solution for automated code review.

notes.title: page-agent
notes.ai_summary: Page Agent is a lightweight JavaScript library that embeds an AI agent directly into any web page, enabling natural language control of the UI without requiring browser extensions, headless browsers, or multimodal LLMs. It uses text-based DOM manipulation and supports any LLM, making it a versatile tool for building AI copilots, automating form filling, and improving accessibility. Backed by Alibaba and actively maintained, it offers easy integration via a single script tag and optional Chrome extension for multi-page tasks.

notes.title: AstrBot

notes.title: video-use
notes.ai_summary: video-use is an open-source tool that leverages Claude Code to edit videos through natural language chats. It automates tasks like cutting filler words, color grading, adding subtitles, and generating animations, making video editing accessible via coding agents. notes.title: OpenMontage
notes.ai_summary: OpenMontage is the first open-source, agentic video production system, enabling developers to use AI coding assistants to create videos through 12 pipelines and over 700 agent skill and production-knowledge files. It integrates multiple AI models and tools into a unified, agent-driven workflow for research, scripting, asset generation, editing, and final composition. This project is significant for democratizing AI-powered video production and providing a modular, extensible framework.

notes.title: WrenAI
notes.ai_summary: WrenAI is an open-source generative BI engine that enables AI agents to produce governed dashboards and SQL from natural language, covering 22+ data sources. It distinguishes itself by providing a context layer that injects business semantics and governance into the generation process, making AI-driven BI trustworthy. This project is highly relevant for developers building agentic data applications.

notes.title: openpilot
notes.ai_summary: openpilot is an open-source operating system for robotics, primarily used to upgrade driver assistance systems in over 300 supported cars. This project is a leading example of open-source autonomous vehicle technology, with active development and strong community support.

notes.ai_summary: MediaCrawler 是一款基于 Playwright 的多平台自媒体数据采集工具，支持小红书、抖音、快手、B 站、微博、贴吧、知乎等主流平台，无需 JS 逆向即可抓取公开内容，适合学习爬虫技术和数据采集。该项目功能全面且维护活跃，但使用者需注意法律合规性，仅限学习用途。

todo_items.text: 完善英文文档和国际化支持，降低海外开发者使用门槛
增加更多平台的适配（如微信视频号、知乎专栏等），保持工具覆盖面
增强异常处理与断点续爬功能（现有 Pro 版已提供，但开源版可考虑基础实现）
补充单元测试和集成测试，提高代码健壮性
明确指引用户如何合规使用（如 robots.txt、频率控制），避免法律风险

notes.title: MinerU
notes.ai_summary: MinerU transforms complex documents like PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX into LLM-ready Markdown or JSON, streamlining data extraction for agentic and RAG workflows. With built-in OCR, layout analysis, and batch processing, it significantly reduces the overhead of preparing document data for AI applications.

todo_items.text: Evaluate processing speed and accuracy for large PDF files
Try web demo or HuggingFace demo to test output quality
Integrate with a RAG pipeline (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex) as a document loader
Review CLI and PyPI installation for local usage
Check support for complex table structures and multilingual OCR

notes.title: Chat2DB
notes.ai_summary: Chat2DB is a free, cross-platform AI-powered database client and SQL workspace supporting over 30 databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL, and ClickHouse. It combines a full-featured SQL editor with an AI assistant for natural language querying, optimization, and explanation, making it a powerful tool for developers, DBAs, and data teams.

todo_items.text: Enhance AI model integration to support more custom models and fine-tuning
Improve cross-platform performance and stability, especially on Linux
Add more advanced BI dashboard features and chart types
Expand plugin system to cover additional niche databases
Provide more comprehensive documentation and tutorials for beginners
Implement collaborative features for team-based SQL editing and sharing

notes.title: impeccable
notes.ai_summary: Impeccable is a design guidance tool for AI coding agents, offering 23 commands and 60 deterministic detector rules to improve AI-generated frontend design. It helps developers avoid cookie-cutter patterns and achieve polished, brand-aligned interfaces through structured critiques, live browser iteration, and configurable design context.

todo_items.text: Run `/impeccable init` in your project to set up design context (PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md)
Explore the 23 commands like `critique`, `audit`, `polish` to refine AI-generated designs
Test the CLI and browser extension with the 60 deterministic detector rules (no LLM needed)
Read the full documentation at impeccable.style for advanced usage and pinning commands
Contribute additional detector rules or commands to expand the project

notes.title: awesome-mcp-servers
notes.ai_summary: This is a curated list of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, providing developers with a comprehensive directory of server implementations to extend AI capabilities through file access, database connections, API integrations, and more. It is an essential resource for anyone building with MCP, offering clear categorization, community links, and a synced web directory.

todo_items.text: Review the list to identify MCP servers relevant to your project and test them.
Contribute a new MCP server or update existing entries if you maintain one.
Check the synced web directory at glama.ai for a more interactive browsing experience.
Join the community Discord or Reddit to discuss MCP servers and best practices.

notes.title: free-for-dev

It saves significant time by aggregating over 1,600 contributions into a single reference, making it an essential resource for building infrastructure on a budget.

Review and merge pending pull requests for new services or updates to existing entries
Add a section for free tiers of generative AI and ML platforms to reflect current trends

notes.title: supervision
notes.ai_summary: Supervision is a model-agnostic Python library that provides reusable tools for computer vision, including detection, segmentation, tracking, and annotation. It simplifies building CV applications by offering pre-built annotators, dataset loaders, and seamless integrations with popular models like Ultralytics, Transformers, and Inference. This library is essential for developers looking to accelerate their computer vision workflows.

todo_items.text: Install the supervision package and run the quickstart examples to understand the API.
Integrate a model (e.g., Ultralytics YOLO) with supervision's Detections API for object detection.
Explore the documentation and tutorials to learn about advanced features like zone counting and annotation tools.
Contribute to the repository by reporting issues or submitting pull requests to improve the library.
Bookmark the project as a reference for future computer vision projects.

notes.title: code-review-graph
notes.ai_summary: code-review-graph is a local-first tool that builds a persistent knowledge graph of your codebase using Tree-sitter, enabling AI coding tools to access only relevant context during code reviews. By reducing token consumption dramatically (38x to 528x), it makes AI-assisted reviews faster and cheaper for large repositories. It supports MCP protocol and CLI usage, making it easy to integrate with tools like Claude Code.

todo_items.text: Install and try on a small project to verify token reduction benefits
Integrate into your AI coding workflow (e.g., Claude Code or other MCP-compatible assistants)
Explore documentation and commands to understand all features
Contribute to the roadmap or open issues for missing language support
Run provided benchmarks on your own repos to measure expected savings

notes.title: attu
notes.ai_summary: Attu is an AI-native management GUI for Milvus vector databases, providing a unified web/desktop interface for browsing collections, running vector searches, managing backups, monitoring cluster health, and interacting with an LLM-powered assistant. Its v3 rewrite with modern stack and features like backup/restore, task management, and REST API playground makes it essential for Milvus users.

todo_items.text: Add support for more embedding providers beyond the current ones
Improve AI agent reliability and expand skill set for complex queries
Enhance incremental backup performance and compression options
Integrate with Milvus 2.4+ new features like floating point quantization
Add dark/light theme persistence and system preference detection
Provide more detailed documentation for REST API playground endpoints

notes.title: OpenMAIC
notes.ai_summary: OpenMAIC is an open-source, immersive multi-agent interactive classroom platform that leverages LLMs to create realistic multi-agent learning experiences. Built with TypeScript, Next.js, and LangGraph, it supports one-click deployment, video export, project-based learning, and integration with various AI providers, making it valuable for educators, researchers, and AI developers.

todo_items.text: Explore the live demo at open.maic.chat to get a hands-on feel for the platform.
Check the @openmaic/* SDK family on npm for integrating OpenMAIC into your own projects.
Deploy your own instance using the Vercel one-click deploy button with your LLM API keys.
Review the published paper (JCST 2026) for academic context and technical details.
Contribute to the project by reporting issues or submitting pull requests on GitHub.
